draft.article: Miami families have multiple free community celebrations to gather Halloween candy this weekend. The festivities start Friday, October 30, from 6 to 9:30 p.m. at Shenandoah Park with a trunk-or-treat trail and carnival snacks. On Saturday, October 31, afternoon events include Coral Gables trick-or-treating along Miracle Mile starting at 2 p.m. with a dog costume contest, plus South Miami Safe Streets on Sunset Drive from 4 to 7 p.m. featuring allergy-friendly candy stations. Evening options kick off at 6 p.m. with trunk-or-treat games at Milander Park in Hialeah and Fuller Street festivities in Coconut Grove. Lincoln Road in Miami Beach also hosts costume strolls from 5 p.m. into the night.

Coastal flood warnings covered Miami-Dade and Broward counties alongside an 11 a.m. wind advisory and gale warnings over South Florida waters. Over the weekend, rising tides flooded streets near Northeast 79th Street and Tenth Avenue in Miami, as well as Bill Baggs Cape Florida State Park in Key Biscayne. Powerful gusts paired with a full moon forced waves over barriers along the Hollywood Beach Broadwalk, where local shops stacked sandbags. A local artist displayed sculptures directly on flooded Miami Beach sidewalks to draw attention to rising sea levels.

headlines: MIAMI-DADE OFFICE MARKET FACES HIGH RENTS AND SLOWING DEALS
BRICKELL OFFICE RENTS REACH RECORD HIGHS
ARE MIAMI-DADE OFFICE BUILDINGS FINALLY BACK FIVE YEARS LATER?
draft.article: Five years after the pandemic altered workspaces, analysts Peter Zalewski and Oscar Musibay examined whether Miami-Dade office buildings have truly recovered. Their assessment reviews vacancy numbers alongside shifting business demands across local neighborhoods. Brickell continues to see record-high rents, setting a sharp contrast with the downtown core. Meanwhile, interest rates and the election cycle have slowed leasing activity throughout the county. Activity remains split across Class A hubs like Coral Gables, Coconut Grove, and Aventura. At the same time, specialized leasing is expanding, with medical and med spa spaces gaining ground across submarkets like Edgewater, the Design District, and Little Haiti.

PUBLIX BUYS ITS MIAMI-DADE SHOPPING PLAZAS
SUPERMARKET GIANT BECOMES THE LANDLORD ACROSS MIAMI-DADE CENTERS
draft.article: Lakeland-based Publix is making major real estate moves across Miami-Dade by taking ownership of the shopping centers where it operates. During October, the grocery giant invested $107 million to purchase two retail centers in the county. The newly acquired commercial plazas are located near Miami International Airport and in southwest Miami-Dade. With these purchases, the supermarket giant is shifting its position from a retail tenant into a commercial landlord. Publix now owns the shopping plazas where its own supermarkets anchor the retail mix.

headlines: TEEN CHARGED AFTER 12 HURT IN FAMU HOMECOMING SHOOTING
FLORIDA REELS AFTER MASS SHOOTING OUTSIDE FOOTBALL STADIUM
STATEWIDE VIOLENCE CRISIS GROWS WITH LATEST FLORIDA MASS SHOOTING
draft.article:
South Floridians are watching closely as another mass tragedy impacts the state. Gunfire erupted outside Bragg Memorial Stadium following the Florida A&M Homecoming game in Tallahassee on October 24.

Tallahassee police reported that 12 people were injured, including six children. The youngest victim was 11 years old. A shooting victim's grandmother was also hurt while fleeing the chaos.

Officers arrested a 15-year-old boy on October 25, charging him with 11 counts of attempted homicide and possession of a firearm by a delinquent.

This incident marks the 21st mass shooting in Florida this year, reviving painful memories across South Florida of previous state tragedies, including the 2018 massacre at Parkland's Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School.

Defensively, Marquise Lightfoot registered four quarterback pressures, while JJ Dunnigan forced a fumble that Justin Scott recovered to secure the home triumph.
